questions.prompt: What does exercise physiology mainly study?
options: How body systems respond and adapt to physical activity
How medals are arranged after a tournament
How team uniforms are designed
How spectators choose favourite players
questions.correctAnswer: How body systems respond and adapt to physical activity
questions.explanation: Exercise physiology explains changes in body systems during and after activity. It helps learners connect training with performance and health.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe exercise physiology as the study of body responses to physical activity.

questions.prompt: Which fitness component is most closely linked to sustained running, swimming, or cycling?
options: Cardiorespiratory endurance
Static balance only
Reaction time only
Body composition only
questions.correctAnswer: Cardiorespiratory endurance
questions.explanation: Cardiorespiratory endurance allows the heart, lungs, and blood vessels to support activity for an extended time. It is central to many endurance events.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cardiorespiratory endurance as a key fitness component for sustained activity.

questions.prompt: What is the role of ATP in muscle contraction?
options: It supplies immediate usable energy for muscle work
It stores match scores for officials
It protects shoes from friction
It decides the rules of a sport
questions.correctAnswer: It supplies immediate usable energy for muscle work
questions.explanation: ATP is the immediate energy source used by muscle fibres. The body must continually resynthesise ATP during activity.
questions.learningOutcome: State the function of ATP during muscular activity.

questions.prompt: Which energy system is dominant during a very short explosive start in a sprint?
options: ATP-PC system
Aerobic system only
Digestive system
Long-term fat storage system
questions.correctAnswer: ATP-PC system
questions.explanation: The ATP-PC system supplies rapid energy for very short, high-intensity actions. It is important in starts, jumps, and throws.
questions.learningOutcome: Name the energy system used for short explosive actions.

questions.prompt: Which body response usually rises immediately when exercise intensity increases?
options: Heart rate
Shoe size
Arm span
Number of team substitutes
questions.correctAnswer: Heart rate
questions.explanation: Heart rate rises to deliver more oxygen and nutrients to working muscles. It is a simple way to observe exercise intensity.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise heart rate as an immediate response to increased exercise intensity.

questions.prompt: What does biomechanics focus on in sports science?
options: Forces and movement in human performance
Drawing fixture posters only
Counting spectators at a match
Naming sports celebrities
questions.correctAnswer: Forces and movement in human performance
questions.explanation: Biomechanics applies physics to movement. It helps explain efficient, safe, and effective techniques.
questions.learningOutcome: Define biomechanics in relation to sports performance.

questions.prompt: In sprinting, what does stride frequency mean?
options: The number of strides taken in a given time
The colour of lane markings
The height of the starting blocks
The total number of races in a season
questions.correctAnswer: The number of strides taken in a given time
questions.explanation: Stride frequency is how quickly an athlete cycles through strides. Sprint speed depends on both stride frequency and stride length.
questions.learningOutcome: State the meaning of stride frequency in sprint performance.

questions.prompt: Which macronutrient is the main fuel source for high-intensity games and training?
options: Carbohydrate
Water
Calcium
Fibre only
questions.correctAnswer: Carbohydrate
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate is stored as glycogen and supports intense activity. A balanced diet also includes protein, fats, vitamins, minerals, and water.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify carbohydrate as a major energy source for high-intensity activity.

questions.prompt: What is dehydration in a sports context?
options: Loss of body water that can reduce performance and safety
A planned rest day after competition
A method of increasing stride length
A way of marking a playing area
questions.correctAnswer: Loss of body water that can reduce performance and safety
questions.explanation: Dehydration occurs when fluid loss is not replaced adequately. It can affect concentration, temperature regulation, and performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Define dehydration and its relevance to sports participation.

questions.prompt: What is a sprain?
options: An injury to a ligament around a joint
A tear in a match fixture list
A planned training cycle
A type of tournament draw
questions.correctAnswer: An injury to a ligament around a joint
questions.explanation: A sprain affects ligaments, which connect bones at joints. It is different from a muscle or tendon strain.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a sprain as a ligament injury.

questions.prompt: Which training principle means activities should match the demands of the target sport or event?
options: Specificity
Randomness
Decoration
Spectatorship
questions.correctAnswer: Specificity
questions.explanation: Specificity means training should reflect the muscles, movements, energy systems, and skills needed in performance. It helps make practice purposeful.
questions.learningOutcome: Name specificity as a principle used when planning training.

questions.prompt: Which quality should guide an official when applying rules during a match?
options: Impartiality
Favouritism
Guesswork
Intimidation
questions.correctAnswer: Impartiality
questions.explanation: Impartiality means applying rules fairly to all participants. It supports trust, safety, and respect in competition.
questions.learningOutcome: State impartiality as a key quality of sports officiating.

questions.prompt: What does a SMART goal include?
options: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound features
Speed, medals, applause, ranking, and trophies
Stretching, marking, aiming, running, and timing only
Slogans, music, awards, rewards, and travel
questions.correctAnswer: Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound features
questions.explanation: SMART goals make progress easier to plan and review. They turn broad wishes into clear targets.
questions.learningOutcome: Recall the features of a SMART performance goal.

questions.prompt: What does fair play mean in sport?
options: Competing honestly while respecting rules, opponents, and officials
Winning by any method available
Ignoring safety rules when spectators are excited
Changing scores to help friends
questions.correctAnswer: Competing honestly while respecting rules, opponents, and officials
questions.explanation: Fair play joins honesty, respect, and responsibility. It protects both the spirit and rules of sport.
questions.learningOutcome: Define fair play in school and community sport.

questions.prompt: Which feature describes a round-robin tournament?
options: Each team or player competes against every other team or player
One loss removes a team immediately
Only the fastest team plays all fixtures
The final ranking is decided before play starts
questions.correctAnswer: Each team or player competes against every other team or player
questions.explanation: A round-robin format gives every participant several fixtures. It is useful when organisers want broad participation and fair comparison.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the main feature of a round-robin tournament.

questions.prompt: Why is a progressive warm-up useful before vigorous sport?
options: It raises body temperature and prepares joints, muscles, and nerves for activity
It guarantees victory before the game begins
It replaces all technical practice
It removes the need to drink water all day
questions.correctAnswer: It raises body temperature and prepares joints, muscles, and nerves for activity
questions.explanation: A warm-up gradually prepares the body for greater intensity. It can improve readiness and reduce avoidable injury risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of a progressive warm-up before vigorous activity.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes aerobic from anaerobic energy production?
options: Aerobic energy uses oxygen for sustained work, while anaerobic energy supports short intense work without oxygen as the main pathway
Aerobic energy only works during sleep, while anaerobic energy only works during reading
Both systems are unrelated to movement
Anaerobic energy is always slower than aerobic energy in explosive actions
questions.correctAnswer: Aerobic energy uses oxygen for sustained work, while anaerobic energy supports short intense work without oxygen as the main pathway
questions.explanation: Both systems contribute during sport, but their dominance changes with intensity and duration. Endurance events rely more on aerobic energy.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the basic difference between aerobic and anaerobic energy pathways.

questions.prompt: Why is stroke volume important during endurance activity?
options: It affects how much blood the heart pumps with each beat
It records the number of penalties in a game
It measures the width of a lane
It shows the colour of an athlete's kit
questions.correctAnswer: It affects how much blood the heart pumps with each beat
questions.explanation: Stroke volume is the amount of blood pumped per heartbeat. Higher effective pumping supports oxygen delivery during endurance work.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain stroke volume as part of cardiovascular function during exercise.

questions.prompt: Which observation can suggest improved cardiorespiratory fitness after several weeks of training?
options: A lower recovery heart rate after the same running task
A larger shoe size after every session
More spelling errors on a score sheet
A shorter warm-up with higher injury risk
questions.correctAnswer: A lower recovery heart rate after the same running task
questions.explanation: Fitter athletes often recover more efficiently from the same workload. Heart rate recovery is one useful monitoring sign.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple signs of improved cardiorespiratory fitness.

questions.prompt: Why is rating of perceived exertion useful during training?
options: It helps learners estimate how hard the session feels
It replaces all safety supervision
It measures the exact mass of equipment
It decides tournament fixtures automatically
questions.correctAnswer: It helps learners estimate how hard the session feels
questions.explanation: Perceived exertion gives a quick subjective guide to intensity. It can be combined with heart rate, pace, and coach observation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how perceived exertion can help monitor exercise intensity.

questions.prompt: Why should learners cool down after hard running?
options: It helps the body return gradually toward resting state and supports recovery
It makes muscles stronger without training
It cancels the need for sleep
It changes a sprint into a throwing event
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the body return gradually toward resting state and supports recovery
questions.explanation: A cool-down lowers intensity gradually and can include gentle movement and stretching. It supports comfort and recovery after effort.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of cool-down activities after vigorous exercise.

questions.prompt: When a sprinter pushes backward against the track and moves forward, which principle is being shown?
options: For every action force there is an opposite reaction force
A heavier whistle makes a runner faster
Only gravity creates horizontal speed
Movement happens without force
questions.correctAnswer: For every action force there is an opposite reaction force
questions.explanation: The athlete applies force backward and downward on the track. The track provides a reaction force that helps drive the athlete forward.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how action and reaction forces contribute to sprinting.

questions.prompt: Which factors mainly affect the flight path of a thrown ball?
options: Release speed, release angle, and release height
Uniform colour, team name, and referee age
Number of spectators, ticket price, and music volume
Size of the score sheet only
questions.correctAnswer: Release speed, release angle, and release height
questions.explanation: Projectile motion depends strongly on how the object is released. Speed, angle, and height shape distance and trajectory.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify release factors that influence projectile flight in sport.

questions.prompt: Why can a lower centre of gravity improve stability in a defensive stance?
options: It makes the body harder to tip outside its base of support
It removes the need for balance
It stops all movement of the legs
It changes body mass into speed
questions.correctAnswer: It makes the body harder to tip outside its base of support
questions.explanation: Stability improves when the centre of gravity is low and the base of support is wide. This helps players resist sudden movement changes.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how centre of gravity affects stability in sport positions.

questions.prompt: How does a good follow-through help in many throwing and striking skills?
options: It allows force to be applied smoothly for longer and improves control
It stops the object before release
It replaces the need to aim
It makes officials ignore technique faults
questions.correctAnswer: It allows force to be applied smoothly for longer and improves control
questions.explanation: Follow-through supports efficient force transfer and controlled deceleration. It is common in throws, kicks, and racket skills.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the performance value of follow-through in sport skills.

questions.prompt: During elbow flexion, the biceps applies effort between the elbow joint and the load in the hand. Which lever class is this?
options: Third-class lever
First-class lever only
Second-class lever only
No lever system
questions.correctAnswer: Third-class lever
questions.explanation: In a third-class lever, the effort lies between the fulcrum and the load. Many human limb movements use this arrangement.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify a third-class lever in a common body movement.

questions.prompt: Why do suitable studs or spikes improve movement on some sports surfaces?
options: They increase grip by improving friction between footwear and the surface
They make the athlete immune to fatigue
They reduce all need for skill
They lower the rules of the event
questions.correctAnswer: They increase grip by improving friction between footwear and the surface
questions.explanation: Appropriate footwear can improve traction and reduce slipping. The choice should match the surface and activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how friction affects movement and safety in sport.

questions.prompt: Why is neutral spine alignment encouraged when lifting training equipment?
options: It helps distribute load more safely through the body
It makes the equipment weight disappear
It prevents all tiredness after training
It changes lifting into officiating
questions.correctAnswer: It helps distribute load more safely through the body
questions.explanation: Good alignment supports controlled movement and reduces unnecessary stress. Learners should use suitable loads and supervision.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why body alignment matters during resistance activities.

questions.prompt: Why is progressive overload used in training?
options: It challenges the body gradually so adaptation can occur
It means every session must be maximal
It removes the need for recovery
It avoids all measurement of progress
questions.correctAnswer: It challenges the body gradually so adaptation can occur
questions.explanation: Progressive overload increases training demand in controlled steps. This helps improve fitness while managing injury risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain progressive overload as a training principle.

questions.prompt: What does reversibility mean in sports training?
options: Fitness gains may reduce when training is stopped for a long period
Every athlete improves without practice
Skills become permanent after one lesson
Recovery days are never needed
questions.correctAnswer: Fitness gains may reduce when training is stopped for a long period
questions.explanation: The body adapts to the demands placed on it. If training is removed, some adaptations can gradually decline.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the principle of reversibility in training.

questions.prompt: What is periodisation in a training programme?
options: Dividing training into planned phases with different goals and recovery
Training randomly every day without records
Replacing practice with only speeches
Holding every competition on the same day
questions.correctAnswer: Dividing training into planned phases with different goals and recovery
questions.explanation: Periodisation organises workload over time. It helps athletes build, peak, and recover at suitable stages.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe periodisation as planned training phases over time.

questions.prompt: Why should a training plan include recovery days?
options: They allow adaptation and reduce excessive fatigue
They make practice unnecessary forever
They prevent learners from ever sweating
They are only for recording scores
questions.correctAnswer: They allow adaptation and reduce excessive fatigue
questions.explanation: Training stresses the body, while recovery helps the body adapt. Without recovery, performance and safety can suffer.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of recovery in a balanced training programme.

questions.prompt: What is a key role of protein in sports nutrition?
options: Supporting growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues
Replacing oxygen in the lungs
Preventing all forms of fatigue instantly
Changing rules during a match
questions.correctAnswer: Supporting growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues
questions.explanation: Protein helps repair and maintain body tissues after normal activity and training. It works best as part of a balanced diet.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of protein in growth and tissue repair for active learners.

questions.prompt: Why are carbohydrate-rich foods useful before prolonged or intense activity?
options: They help maintain glycogen stores used for energy
They make water unnecessary
They replace all warm-up activities
They stop the need for sleep
questions.correctAnswer: They help maintain glycogen stores used for energy
questions.explanation: Carbohydrate is stored as glycogen in muscles and the liver. These stores help fuel moderate to high intensity exercise.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why carbohydrate supports energy supply during sport.

questions.prompt: Why are electrolytes relevant during long sessions in hot conditions?
options: They help with fluid balance and normal nerve and muscle function
They replace all coaching feedback
They decide the winner of a match
They remove the need to practise skills
questions.correctAnswer: They help with fluid balance and normal nerve and muscle function
questions.explanation: Sweat contains water and electrolytes. During long or hot sessions, replacing fluids appropriately supports safe participation.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the basic role of electrolytes during prolonged physical activity.

questions.prompt: Which eating practice is generally sensible before a school competition?
options: Eat familiar balanced food well before activity and avoid a heavy meal just before play
Try unfamiliar foods immediately before the start
Skip all food and water for the whole day
Eat only sweets because they replace training
questions.correctAnswer: Eat familiar balanced food well before activity and avoid a heavy meal just before play
questions.explanation: Familiar balanced foods reduce the chance of discomfort and provide useful energy. Heavy meals immediately before activity can feel uncomfortable.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain practical pre-event eating choices for school sport.

questions.prompt: Why does adequate sleep support sport performance?
options: It supports recovery, learning, concentration, and energy regulation
It replaces all physical conditioning
It guarantees that injuries cannot occur
It changes an athlete's age group
questions.correctAnswer: It supports recovery, learning, concentration, and energy regulation
questions.explanation: Sleep helps the body and brain recover from daily demands. It also supports attention and skill learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of sleep as part of recovery for active learners.

questions.prompt: Why is risk assessment done before a sports activity?
options: To identify hazards and plan controls that reduce harm
To make the activity more secret
To avoid writing any safety plan
To choose winners before competition
questions.correctAnswer: To identify hazards and plan controls that reduce harm
questions.explanation: Risk assessment checks equipment, environment, participants, and supervision. It helps organisers prepare safer activities.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why risk assessment is used before sport and recreation activities.

questions.prompt: What is an overuse injury?
options: An injury linked to repeated stress without enough recovery
A planned rest day in a training cycle
A medal awarded for attendance
A whistle signal used by officials
questions.correctAnswer: An injury linked to repeated stress without enough recovery
questions.explanation: Overuse injuries often develop gradually from repeated loading. Training load, technique, footwear, and recovery can all contribute.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain overuse injury as a risk of repeated load without adequate recovery.

questions.prompt: Why should coaches keep simple records of attendance, workload, and progress?
options: Records help monitor improvement, fatigue, and training decisions
Records make physical practice unnecessary
Records should replace all observation
Records are only useful after a trophy is won
questions.correctAnswer: Records help monitor improvement, fatigue, and training decisions
questions.explanation: Training records show patterns over time. They support fair feedback and safer planning.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why training records support coaching decisions.

questions.prompt: An athlete has a resting heart rate of 60 beats per minute and an estimated maximum heart rate of 200 beats per minute. What is the heart rate reserve?
options: 140 beats per minute
260 beats per minute
120 beats per minute
80 beats per minute
questions.correctAnswer: 140 beats per minute
questions.explanation: Heart rate reserve is estimated maximum heart rate minus resting heart rate. Here, 200 minus 60 equals 140 beats per minute.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate heart rate reserve from resting and estimated maximum heart rate values.

questions.prompt: A 400 metre runner feels heavy leg fatigue near the end of a fast race. Which energy explanation is most suitable?
options: Anaerobic glycolysis is contributing strongly, with aerobic support also present
Only the ATP-PC system supplies energy for the whole race
No energy system is involved once fatigue begins
Digestion is the only source of race speed
questions.correctAnswer: Anaerobic glycolysis is contributing strongly, with aerobic support also present
questions.explanation: A fast 400 metre race needs high-intensity energy for longer than the ATP-PC system can support alone. Both anaerobic and aerobic pathways contribute.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply energy system knowledge to a middle-distance sprint event.

questions.prompt: Which training method best supports a learner preparing for a 5 kilometre run?
options: Regular continuous runs and tempo efforts at controlled intensity
Only one maximal jump each week
Only static stretching with no running
Only reaction games lasting one second
questions.correctAnswer: Regular continuous runs and tempo efforts at controlled intensity
questions.explanation: A 5 kilometre run depends mainly on aerobic endurance and pacing. Continuous and tempo work can develop these qualities progressively.
questions.learningOutcome: Select training methods that match endurance event demands.

questions.prompt: A netball player performs well early but repeatedly slows down in the final quarter. Which training focus is most relevant?
options: Game-specific endurance using intervals and recovery practice
Only handwriting speed
Avoiding all movement during training
Changing bib colours after each pass
questions.correctAnswer: Game-specific endurance using intervals and recovery practice
questions.explanation: Netball requires repeated high-intensity movement with short recoveries. Training should reflect those game demands.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply specificity when choosing conditioning for team games.

questions.prompt: During a moderate endurance run, a learner cannot speak short phrases without gasping. What adjustment is most suitable?
options: Reduce pace until breathing and speech become more controlled
Sprint faster until the session ends
Hold the breath to save energy
Stop using warm-ups permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce pace until breathing and speech become more controlled
questions.explanation: The talk test helps estimate exercise intensity. If speech is very difficult during a moderate session, the pace is probably too high.
questions.learningOutcome: Use the talk test to adjust endurance training intensity.

questions.prompt: A class repeats a sit-up test after six weeks. Which step makes comparison with the first test more reliable?
options: Use the same protocol, time limit, and scoring rules
Change the test time and counting method
Allow different learners to choose different rules
Record only the highest score from memory
questions.correctAnswer: Use the same protocol, time limit, and scoring rules
questions.explanation: Reliable comparison needs consistent procedures. Changing the protocol makes progress harder to interpret.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply reliability principles when comparing fitness test results.

questions.prompt: A learner's javelin throw is powerful but the release angle is very low. Which coaching cue is most useful?
options: Practise a controlled release path that sends the javelin forward and upward safely
Throw harder into the ground
Ignore run-up rhythm and only shout louder
Release behind the body to increase distance
questions.correctAnswer: Practise a controlled release path that sends the javelin forward and upward safely
questions.explanation: Projectile distance depends on force and release conditions. A very low release angle can limit flight time and distance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply projectile principles to improve a throwing technique.

questions.prompt: A long jumper lands with stiff knees and loses balance. Which feedback best supports safer landing?
options: Land with controlled knee flexion and keep the body balanced forward
Lock the knees harder on contact
Look backward during landing
Place the hands behind the body before the feet land
questions.correctAnswer: Land with controlled knee flexion and keep the body balanced forward
questions.explanation: Controlled knee flexion helps absorb force. Good landing mechanics improve safety and reduce loss of distance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe landing principles to jumping performance.

questions.prompt: A basketball defender wants to improve quick changes of direction. Which drill is most relevant?
options: Cone shuttles with controlled acceleration, deceleration, and side steps
A long slow walk with no direction changes
Only sitting toe touches
Copying a fixture table into a notebook
questions.correctAnswer: Cone shuttles with controlled acceleration, deceleration, and side steps
questions.explanation: Agility requires quick direction changes with control. Cone shuttles can practise the movement demands of defending.
questions.learningOutcome: Select an agility drill for court-game movement demands.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports improved vertical jump height for volleyball learners?
options: Progressive leg strength, safe plyometrics, landing practice, and recovery
Only watching videos of elite players
Maximum jumps every day without rest
Skipping warm-up and jumping immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Progressive leg strength, safe plyometrics, landing practice, and recovery
questions.explanation: Jump performance depends on power, technique, and safe landing. Progression and recovery help learners adapt.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply power training principles to volleyball jumping performance.

questions.prompt: A footballer keeps slipping on wet grass during training. Which decision best addresses the biomechanical issue?
options: Check the surface and use suitable footwear with appropriate grip
Run faster without changing anything
Remove warm-up from the session
Choose players by shoe colour
questions.correctAnswer: Check the surface and use suitable footwear with appropriate grip
questions.explanation: Slipping often relates to poor traction between footwear and surface. Surface inspection and suitable footwear can improve safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply friction principles to a sports safety decision.

questions.prompt: A shot putter drives from the legs, rotates the trunk, and then pushes with the arm. Which biomechanical idea is being used?
options: Sequential summation of forces
Random movement without coordination
Static balance only
Reversibility of training
questions.correctAnswer: Sequential summation of forces
questions.explanation: Many powerful skills transfer force from larger body segments to smaller segments in sequence. This can improve release speed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply force summation to a throwing event technique.

questions.prompt: A runner increases weekly distance from 10 kilometres to 18 kilometres in one week and develops persistent soreness. What is the training problem?
options: The overload increased too quickly for safe adaptation
The runner used too much specificity
The athlete had too many recovery records
The warm-up was too gradual
questions.correctAnswer: The overload increased too quickly for safe adaptation
questions.explanation: Large sudden increases in training load can overload tissues. Progression should be gradual and responsive to recovery.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply progression principles to identify unsafe training load changes.

questions.prompt: Which FITT plan best targets flexibility improvement?
options: Stretch regularly, use gentle tension, hold for suitable time, and select relevant muscle groups
Sprint once a month at maximum speed
Lift the heaviest possible load every lesson
Only record scores without movement
questions.correctAnswer: Stretch regularly, use gentle tension, hold for suitable time, and select relevant muscle groups
questions.explanation: FITT refers to frequency, intensity, time, and type. A flexibility plan should apply these variables safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply the FITT principle to a flexibility programme.

questions.prompt: A school athletics team has an important competition next week. Which tapering choice is most suitable?
options: Reduce total training volume while keeping some event-specific intensity
Double every training load until competition day
Stop all movement for the whole week
Replace practice with only uniform inspection
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce total training volume while keeping some event-specific intensity
questions.explanation: Tapering reduces fatigue while maintaining readiness. It is planned according to event demands and athlete response.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply tapering principles before a competition.

questions.prompt: A coach wants to compare 30 metre sprint times from March and June. Which approach gives the fairest comparison?
options: Use the same distance, start method, timing method, and surface
Change the distance and timing device for the second test
Let one group start running before the signal
Estimate all times without recording them
questions.correctAnswer: Use the same distance, start method, timing method, and surface
questions.explanation: Consistent conditions improve the usefulness of performance comparisons. Changing key conditions can hide or exaggerate progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply standardisation when comparing repeated sprint test results.

questions.prompt: A school has limited gym equipment. Which strength circuit is safest and most practical?
options: Body-weight squats, press-ups, planks, and supervised use of light improvised loads
Unknown heavy loads lifted without instruction
Only maximal lifts by beginners
Throwing equipment randomly across the field
questions.correctAnswer: Body-weight squats, press-ups, planks, and supervised use of light improvised loads
questions.explanation: Safe strength work can use body weight and simple equipment. Supervision, technique, and suitable loads matter more than expensive facilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a safe basic strength circuit using available resources.

questions.prompt: Which practice structure best helps beginners learn a basketball lay-up?
options: Demonstrate, practise parts of the movement, give feedback, then combine the skill
Start with full-speed contact under pressure only
Avoid feedback until the end of the term
Practise only free throws and never approach the basket
questions.correctAnswer: Demonstrate, practise parts of the movement, give feedback, then combine the skill
questions.explanation: Complex skills can be learned through demonstration, part practice, and feedback. Learners then progress toward game-like practice.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply part-practice and feedback to learning a sport skill.

questions.prompt: Which hydration plan is most suitable for a long training session in hot weather?
options: Drink water before, during, and after activity, use shade breaks, and monitor how learners feel
Avoid all fluids until training is finished
Drink only when dizziness becomes severe
Replace water with extra sprint repetitions
questions.correctAnswer: Drink water before, during, and after activity, use shade breaks, and monitor how learners feel
questions.explanation: Hot conditions increase fluid loss and heat strain. Planned drinking opportunities and shade breaks support safer participation.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply hydration principles to training in hot conditions.

questions.prompt: A learner develops muscle cramps during a hot training session. Which first response is most appropriate at school level?
options: Stop activity, rest in shade, drink fluids if able, and inform the teacher or coach
Continue sprinting until the cramps disappear
Hide the problem from the coach
Start a new high-intensity drill immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Stop activity, rest in shade, drink fluids if able, and inform the teacher or coach
questions.explanation: Stopping activity and alerting supervision supports safety. Persistent or severe symptoms need help from a qualified health professional.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe school-level responses to heat-related discomfort during sport.

questions.prompt: A learner twists an ankle and cannot continue safely. Which immediate response is most suitable?
options: Stop participation, support the ankle, use a wrapped cold pack if available, and seek help
Force the learner to finish the session
Massage hard and return to play immediately
Ignore swelling because it is always harmless
questions.correctAnswer: Stop participation, support the ankle, use a wrapped cold pack if available, and seek help
questions.explanation: The priority is to prevent further harm and get appropriate assistance. Learners should not be pushed back into play after a painful injury.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic first aid principles to a suspected ankle sprain.

questions.prompt: A player is dazed after a head collision and seems confused. What should happen first?
options: Remove the player from play and seek medical assessment through the responsible adult
Tell the player to continue if the score is close
Ask spectators to vote on whether play continues
Give the player a harder drill to test courage
questions.correctAnswer: Remove the player from play and seek medical assessment through the responsible adult
questions.explanation: Confusion after head impact is a serious warning sign. School sport should prioritise removal from play and proper assessment.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe response procedures for suspected concussion signs.

questions.prompt: Which checklist is most useful before a school cross-country event?
options: Route inspection, weather check, water points, first aid, supervision, and communication plan
Only trophy polishing
Only the colour of runners' socks
A list of music to play after the race
questions.correctAnswer: Route inspection, weather check, water points, first aid, supervision, and communication plan
questions.explanation: Cross-country events need route and safety planning. Water, supervision, and communication reduce avoidable risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety planning to a school endurance event.

questions.prompt: A handball player reports repeated shoulder pain after many overarm throws. What should the coach do first?
options: Reduce throwing load, check technique and recovery, and refer for help if pain persists
Increase throwing volume immediately
Tell the player to hide pain from teammates
Replace warm-up with heavier throws
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce throwing load, check technique and recovery, and refer for help if pain persists
questions.explanation: Repeated pain can signal overload or technique problems. Coaches should modify training and involve qualified help when needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe coaching responses to repeated overuse warning signs.

questions.prompt: A learner feels nervous before a race. Which psychological strategy is most suitable?
options: Use controlled breathing, a simple pre-race routine, and positive self-talk
Avoid all preparation and hope anxiety disappears
Insult competitors to feel stronger
Change the race distance without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Use controlled breathing, a simple pre-race routine, and positive self-talk
questions.explanation: Pre-performance routines can help focus attention and manage arousal. Positive self-talk supports confidence and concentration.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic psychological strategies before competition.

questions.prompt: Which goal best improves the vague target, I want to play better?
options: Complete 30 accurate chest passes in three practice sessions by Friday
Become perfect immediately
Try harder someday
Win every match without practice
questions.correctAnswer: Complete 30 accurate chest passes in three practice sessions by Friday
questions.explanation: The selected goal is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound. Clear goals make practice easier to organise.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply SMART criteria to improve a performance goal.

questions.prompt: A coach shows a learner video of their arm action during a tennis serve. What type of support is this?
options: Visual augmented feedback
Genetic selection
Tournament seeding
Energy system testing
questions.correctAnswer: Visual augmented feedback
questions.explanation: Video adds information beyond the learner's own feeling of movement. It can help identify technique points for practice.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify and apply video feedback as augmented feedback in skill learning.

questions.prompt: Which selection method is fairest for choosing a school team?
options: Use clear criteria, open trials, several observations, and recorded evidence
Select only close friends of the captain
Choose players by the cost of their shoes
Pick the first learners who arrive
questions.correctAnswer: Use clear criteria, open trials, several observations, and recorded evidence
questions.explanation: Fair selection needs transparent criteria and more than one source of evidence. This reduces bias and supports development.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply fair procedures when selecting learners for a team.

questions.prompt: Players argue after a disputed foul. What should an official do?
options: Stay calm, use clear signals, apply the rule, and restart play safely
Join the argument loudly
Let spectators decide the foul
Change the rule to please the louder team
questions.correctAnswer: Stay calm, use clear signals, apply the rule, and restart play safely
questions.explanation: Good officiating combines rule knowledge, calm communication, and match control. Consistency helps reduce conflict.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply communication and rule principles during a disputed decision.

questions.prompt: In a single round-robin tournament with 5 teams, how many matches are played?
options: 10 matches
5 matches
15 matches
20 matches
questions.correctAnswer: 10 matches
questions.explanation: Each pairing plays once. The formula n multiplied by n minus 1, divided by 2 gives 5 multiplied by 4, divided by 2, which equals 10.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate fixtures in a single round-robin format.

questions.prompt: After six weeks, a learner runs the same pace with a lower heart rate and faster recovery. What is the best interpretation?
options: Cardiorespiratory efficiency has probably improved
The learner has lost all fitness
The stopwatch is no longer useful
The pace became a throwing skill
questions.correctAnswer: Cardiorespiratory efficiency has probably improved
questions.explanation: Lower heart rate at the same workload can show improved adaptation. Recovery data should be considered with training records and conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse heart rate and recovery patterns as indicators of adaptation.

questions.prompt: Two sprinters run similar times. One has long strides but low stride frequency, while the other has shorter strides but high frequency. What should a coach analyse?
options: The balance between stride length, stride frequency, technique, and relaxation
Only the athlete with longer strides can improve
Stride frequency is never related to speed
Uniform colour determines sprint time
questions.correctAnswer: The balance between stride length, stride frequency, technique, and relaxation
questions.explanation: Sprint speed depends on the relationship between stride length and frequency. Technique changes should preserve efficient rhythm and control.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how stride length and stride frequency interact in sprint performance.

questions.prompt: Why is lactate threshold important for endurance athletes?
options: It relates to the intensity an athlete can sustain before fatigue rises quickly
It is the score needed to win a tournament
It measures only flexibility at the shoulder
It is unrelated to training pace
questions.correctAnswer: It relates to the intensity an athlete can sustain before fatigue rises quickly
questions.explanation: A higher lactate threshold can allow an athlete to sustain a faster pace. Training can target this through controlled endurance work.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the role of lactate threshold in endurance performance.

questions.prompt: An athlete improves vertical jump height but shows little change in a 5 kilometre time trial. Which principle best explains this result?
options: Specificity of training adaptations
All fitness components improve equally
Recovery prevents all improvement
Testing has no value in sport
questions.correctAnswer: Specificity of training adaptations
questions.explanation: Training adaptations are strongest for the systems and movements practised. Power training may not transfer strongly to endurance performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse performance changes using the principle of specificity.

questions.prompt: A sprint warm-up contains only long static stretches and then immediate maximal sprinting. What is the main weakness?
options: It lacks progressive movement and sprint-specific dynamic preparation
It uses too much gradual acceleration
It includes too many reaction starts
It has too much sport-specific rehearsal
questions.correctAnswer: It lacks progressive movement and sprint-specific dynamic preparation
questions.explanation: Sprint preparation should gradually raise intensity and include dynamic movement. Static stretching alone is not a complete warm-up for maximal speed.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate the suitability of a warm-up for sprint performance.

questions.prompt: A training plan schedules hard intervals every day for four weeks with no easier sessions. What is the strongest concern?
options: Insufficient recovery may increase fatigue and injury risk
The plan has too many rest opportunities
The plan is not intense enough for any athlete
Intervals cannot improve performance in any sport
questions.correctAnswer: Insufficient recovery may increase fatigue and injury risk
questions.explanation: Hard sessions need recovery so the body can adapt. Continuous high intensity can increase fatigue and reduce training quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse recovery weaknesses in a training plan.

questions.prompt: Which comparison between open and closed skills is most accurate?
options: A football pass under pressure is more open, while a practised gymnastics sequence is more closed
All skills are closed because rules exist
Open skills happen only indoors
Closed skills require no technique
questions.correctAnswer: A football pass under pressure is more open, while a practised gymnastics sequence is more closed
questions.explanation: Open skills change with the environment and opponents. Closed skills occur in more predictable conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse sport examples using open and closed skill classification.

questions.prompt: Video analysis shows a learner's knees collapsing inward during jump landings. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Reduce jump load, teach knee alignment, and strengthen relevant hip and leg control
Increase jump height immediately
Ignore the pattern because video cannot help
Remove landing practice from every sport
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce jump load, teach knee alignment, and strengthen relevant hip and leg control
questions.explanation: Poor landing alignment can increase injury risk. Technique work, strength, and controlled progression can improve movement quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse movement faults and recommend safe corrective strategies.

questions.prompt: A ball is kicked very high but lands short of the target. What biomechanical adjustment should be considered first?
options: Analyse release angle and speed to produce a more effective flight path
Make the ball heavier during the kick
Remove follow-through from the movement
Kick without looking at the target area
questions.correctAnswer: Analyse release angle and speed to produce a more effective flight path
questions.explanation: A very high trajectory may waste horizontal distance if speed is not used efficiently. Release angle and speed should match the task.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse projectile flight to improve distance or accuracy.

questions.prompt: On a force-time graph, what does a larger area under the curve usually indicate in a movement skill?
options: Greater impulse and a larger change in momentum
Lower effort in every situation
No force was applied
Only better flexibility
questions.correctAnswer: Greater impulse and a larger change in momentum
questions.explanation: Impulse is force applied over time. A larger force-time area can produce a greater change in momentum.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse force-time information using the concept of impulse.

questions.prompt: A learner feels sluggish late in a tournament after skipping breakfast and drinking only soda. What is the best analysis?
options: Energy and hydration choices may be limiting performance and concentration
Skipping breakfast always improves endurance
Soda alone is a complete sports meal
Nutrition cannot affect tournament performance
questions.correctAnswer: Energy and hydration choices may be limiting performance and concentration
questions.explanation: Long tournament days require planned meals, fluids, and recovery. Poor choices can affect energy, comfort, and focus.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how food and fluid choices can affect tournament performance.

questions.prompt: Which situation presents the highest heat stress risk during school sport?
options: Hard training at midday in high heat with little shade and poor fluid access
A cool morning skills lesson with planned water breaks
Light stretching indoors with ventilation
A short rules discussion under shade
questions.correctAnswer: Hard training at midday in high heat with little shade and poor fluid access
questions.explanation: Heat stress risk rises with high temperature, intense activity, limited shade, and inadequate fluids. Organisers should adjust conditions and workload.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse environmental factors that increase heat stress risk.

questions.prompt: Two learners complete the same hard session, but one recovers much more slowly. Which explanation is most reasonable?
options: Recovery can be affected by fitness, sleep, nutrition, stress, and previous training load
All learners must recover at exactly the same speed
Slow recovery proves the session had no effect
Only shoe colour controls recovery
questions.correctAnswer: Recovery can be affected by fitness, sleep, nutrition, stress, and previous training load
questions.explanation: Recovery is individual and influenced by several factors. Coaches should monitor responses rather than assume all athletes adapt equally.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse factors that influence individual recovery from training.

questions.prompt: How should mental imagery be evaluated in skill development?
options: It can improve focus and confidence when combined with physical practice
It fully replaces physical practice in all sports
It only works if no feedback is given
It has no connection to performance preparation
questions.correctAnswer: It can improve focus and confidence when combined with physical practice
questions.explanation: Imagery helps athletes rehearse actions and feelings mentally. It is most useful alongside physical practice and feedback.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate mental imagery as a support for skill learning and performance.

questions.prompt: A team becomes motivated only by prizes and stops practising when rewards are removed. What should the coach consider?
options: Balance external rewards with mastery, enjoyment, and personal progress goals
Use more punishment and remove all feedback
End all goal setting
Make every practice a prize ceremony
questions.correctAnswer: Balance external rewards with mastery, enjoyment, and personal progress goals
questions.explanation: External rewards can help, but long-term motivation also needs ownership, improvement, and enjoyment. Coaches should build intrinsic motivation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how different motivation sources affect sustained participation.

questions.prompt: A coach gives five technical corrections after every attempt, and the learner becomes confused. What is the likely issue?
options: Too much feedback at once can overload attention and reduce learning quality
Learners should never receive feedback
Confusion proves the skill is already mastered
The coach should increase the number of cues
questions.correctAnswer: Too much feedback at once can overload attention and reduce learning quality
questions.explanation: Effective feedback is specific, timely, and manageable. One or two priority cues are often easier for learners to apply.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how feedback quantity affects skill learning.

questions.prompt: Why can talent identification based only on early physical maturity be unfair?
options: It may overlook late developers, skill learning, attitude, and access to training
It is the only reliable way to predict adult performance
It removes all bias from selection
It guarantees equal opportunity for every learner
questions.correctAnswer: It may overlook late developers, skill learning, attitude, and access to training
questions.explanation: Young athletes mature at different rates. Fair talent systems use repeated evidence and consider development potential.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse bias risks in talent identification for adolescent learners.

questions.prompt: Which anti-doping message is most appropriate for school sport education?
options: Substance misuse can harm health, damage fairness, and break sport rules
Winning justifies using any substance
Only elite athletes need ethics
Doping has no effect on trust in sport
questions.correctAnswer: Substance misuse can harm health, damage fairness, and break sport rules
questions.explanation: Anti-doping education protects health and fairness. Learners should ask responsible adults before using unfamiliar supplements or medicines for sport.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse why anti-doping education matters in school and community sport.

questions.prompt: A school has only one afternoon for a large tournament. What is the main trade-off between knockout and round-robin formats?
options: Knockout is faster, while round-robin gives more play and fairer ranking evidence
Round-robin always needs fewer matches than knockout
Knockout guarantees every team the same number of games
Both formats are identical in scheduling
questions.correctAnswer: Knockout is faster, while round-robin gives more play and fairer ranking evidence
questions.explanation: Knockout formats reduce fixtures quickly but eliminate teams after losses. Round-robin formats need more time but provide broader comparison.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse tournament format choices based on time and fairness constraints.

questions.prompt: An event plan lists fixtures and prizes but has no first aid, water, communication, or weather plan. What is the main weakness?
options: It ignores essential participant safety and risk management needs
It has too many safety controls
It gives all teams equal rest
It overuses performance analysis
questions.correctAnswer: It ignores essential participant safety and risk management needs
questions.explanation: Event planning must include safety arrangements as well as competition details. First aid, hydration, communication, and weather planning are practical controls.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safety gaps in a school sports event plan.

questions.prompt: Which one-week microcycle best suits a Grade 11 learner preparing for a 1500 metre race?
options: Aerobic run, interval session, easy recovery, pace practice, mobility, rest, and a controlled time trial
Maximal sprints twice daily with no rest
Only upper-body strength and no running
One race effort every day until competition
questions.correctAnswer: Aerobic run, interval session, easy recovery, pace practice, mobility, rest, and a controlled time trial
questions.explanation: A balanced microcycle includes event-specific work, recovery, and monitoring. The 1500 metre event needs both aerobic capacity and race pace control.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a balanced weekly training structure for a middle-distance runner.

questions.prompt: Which fitness test battery best profiles a football player's main performance needs?
options: Sprint speed, agility, aerobic endurance, lower-body power, flexibility, and football skill observation
Only height and handwriting speed
Only one sit-and-reach test
Only a written quiz on club history
questions.correctAnswer: Sprint speed, agility, aerobic endurance, lower-body power, flexibility, and football skill observation
questions.explanation: Football performance is multidimensional. A useful battery includes physical qualities and sport-specific skill evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a sport-specific fitness testing battery for a team-game athlete.

questions.prompt: Which approach best makes a school invasion-game lesson inclusive for learners with different ability levels?
options: Adapt space, rules, equipment, roles, and challenge while keeping the learning goal clear
Let only the strongest learners touch the ball
Use one fixed task that excludes slower learners
Remove all teamwork from the lesson
questions.correctAnswer: Adapt space, rules, equipment, roles, and challenge while keeping the learning goal clear
questions.explanation: Inclusive teaching adjusts task constraints so more learners can participate meaningfully. The lesson outcome should remain visible.
questions.learningOutcome: Create inclusive adaptations for a practical sports lesson.

questions.prompt: A sprint squad improves times but reports more shin pain and tiredness. What is the best next coaching decision?
options: Review training load, surfaces, footwear, recovery, and technique before increasing intensity
Increase sprint volume because times improved
Ignore pain reports until competition day
Cancel all monitoring and keep the same plan
questions.correctAnswer: Review training load, surfaces, footwear, recovery, and technique before increasing intensity
questions.explanation: Performance gains must be balanced with injury signals. A coach should analyse load and risk factors before progressing.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate training data and injury reports to adjust a performance plan.

questions.prompt: Which research design best tests whether a dynamic warm-up improves 30 metre sprint performance in a class?
options: Use a standard sprint test before and after, control conditions, compare with a usual warm-up group, and record results
Ask only the fastest learner for an opinion
Change the distance every trial and guess the outcome
Test once after a holiday and declare a conclusion
questions.correctAnswer: Use a standard sprint test before and after, control conditions, compare with a usual warm-up group, and record results
questions.explanation: A useful investigation needs comparable testing, controlled conditions, and recorded evidence. A comparison group strengthens the conclusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple controlled investigation for a sports performance question.

questions.prompt: Which injury-prevention programme is most suitable for a basketball team across a term?
options: Dynamic warm-ups, landing mechanics, strength and balance work, load monitoring, equipment checks, and recovery education
Only full-court games with no warm-up
High jumping every day until fatigue is ignored
Removing all technique teaching from practice
questions.correctAnswer: Dynamic warm-ups, landing mechanics, strength and balance work, load monitoring, equipment checks, and recovery education
questions.explanation: Injury prevention works best as a system, not a single drill. Movement quality, load, equipment, and recovery all matter.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a multi-component injury-prevention plan for a team sport.

questions.prompt: Which talent identification system is fairest across schools with different resources?
options: Accessible common tests, repeated observations, coach notes, learner attitude, progress data, and clear selection criteria
Trials that require expensive private equipment
Selection by school reputation only
One secret test with no feedback
questions.correctAnswer: Accessible common tests, repeated observations, coach notes, learner attitude, progress data, and clear selection criteria
questions.explanation: Fair systems reduce resource bias and use several forms of evidence. They should identify both current ability and development potential.
questions.learningOutcome: Design an equitable talent identification system for school sport.

questions.prompt: A player feels pressured to hide an injury so the team can win a final. Which response best reflects ethical sports science practice?
options: Prioritise health, report the concern to the responsible adult, and follow safe return-to-play guidance
Hide the injury because winning is the only goal
Let teammates decide without adult supervision
Use pain as proof of commitment
questions.correctAnswer: Prioritise health, report the concern to the responsible adult, and follow safe return-to-play guidance
questions.explanation: Ethical sport protects participant welfare. Honesty about injury supports safety, trust, and responsible decision-making.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate ethical decisions when performance pressure conflicts with safety.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares a school sports day for safety and smooth running?
options: Assign roles, inspect venues, prepare first aid and water points, schedule events, brief officials, and set communication procedures
Only print certificates and hope activities run themselves
Let each event start whenever participants arrive
Avoid briefing officials so decisions are spontaneous
questions.correctAnswer: Assign roles, inspect venues, prepare first aid and water points, schedule events, brief officials, and set communication procedures
questions.explanation: Good event management combines logistics, safety, and communication. Clear roles help the event run efficiently.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a comprehensive plan for a safe school sports day.

questions.prompt: Which performance-analysis cycle best improves a volleyball serve over several weeks?
options: Collect baseline data, analyse technique, set a target, practise with feedback, retest, and adjust the plan
Guess the problem and never retest
Practise only when the serve already works perfectly
Change every variable at once without records
questions.correctAnswer: Collect baseline data, analyse technique, set a target, practise with feedback, retest, and adjust the plan
questions.explanation: Performance analysis is cyclical. Evidence, targeted practice, feedback, and retesting make improvement easier to track.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a data-informed improvement cycle for a sport skill.
